sentences.text: Misc. Criminal Case No. 37782 of 2025

Ramkrishna
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others

Appearance:
 Shri Rohit Pegwar - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Pradeep Gupta - Govt. Advocate for the respondent/

Order 
This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 63/2023 registered at Police Station - Dehat, District Chhindwara (M.P.)
for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(1), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 5L/6,
5(j)(ii) of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in detention since 16.05.2025.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to revive the prayer for grant of bail after recording the statements of prosecutrix and her parents.

2. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant is that he has taken away the minor prosecutrix and committed rape upon her therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against him.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is in jail since 16.05.2025.
He is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
It is further submitted that now the statements of prosecutrix and her father have been recorded in which they have not supported the prosecution story.
Applicant has no criminal antecedents.
Trial of the case will take considerable time to conclude.
Therefore, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:41974 2 MCRC-37782-2025 it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail pending the trial.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant but fairly submitted that the contraband seized in this case is less than the commercial quantity.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.

Consequently, bail Ramkrishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34864938/
1 application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

sentences.text: 6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
